claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by synchronization of reduction kinetics across all metal precursors.
Rapid surface diffusion at an optimized thermal condition is required for successful homogeneous alloy formation.
Synchronized reduction minimizes differences in reduction potential.
Synchronized reduction causes all metals to nucleate simultaneously.
Simultaneous nucleation promotes homogeneous alloy formation.
Sequential or staggered nucleation leads to phase separation and elemental segregation.
A rapid thermal treatment in a controlled reducing atmosphere can force simultaneous reduction of all metal components within an optimized temperature window.
Rapid heating, a short dwell time, and minimal temperature gradients ensure synchronous precursor reduction and immediate surface diffusion.
Uniform nucleation and immediate surface diffusion generate equilibrated multimetal clusters.
Equilibrated multimetal clusters drive homogeneous alloy formation.
Approximately equal precursor-reduction rates produce nearly simultaneous nucleation and concurrent, well-mixed alloy formation.
Synchronized reduction limits the time available for individual metals to diffuse separately.
Unsynchronized reduction causes staggered nucleation followed by diffusional segregation and phase separation.
Rapid synchronous reduction will produce nanoparticles with homogeneous alloying, minimal phase segregation, and controlled morphology.
Asynchronous reduction will produce elemental segregation, distinct phase boundaries, and uncontrolled morphologies.
Slower or non-optimized heating produces asynchronous nucleation and subsequent phase separation or elemental segregation.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles made by reductive thermal treatments.
The mechanism may not apply to nonthermal chemical-reduction pathways or to systems containing metals with substantially different redox behavior.
The balance between reduction kinetics and surface diffusion depends on composition, precursor coordination, and support interactions.
